ct_blue_trail_section.blurb: This is the main cliff of Webb Mountain Park in western Connecticut, a compact face roughly 40 feet wide and 50 feet tall. It holds a dozen climbs, mostly gear routes and top ropes that run from 5.5 up to 5.9, with the bulk sitting around 5.8. The wall leans just slightly past vertical and is cut by little grooves that give small, sharp crimps, so staying balanced over your feet matters more than raw power. It sticks up a bit above the tree line and catches plenty of sun. A single very hard boulder problem sits off to the left of the cliff.

ct_sativa_slab.blurb: Sativa Slab is a detached slab on the west side of Bald Rock, in Connecticut's Bald Rock Basin bouldering zone. It is a short walk in, around five minutes from the trailhead parking. The twelve problems are all low-angle slab climbs and suit nearly everyone: a couple of VB lines, plenty of V0 and V1, and a handful that reach V3 and V4. It makes a good spot for newer boulderers learning to trust their feet, though stronger climbers will find a few tougher lines.

ct_welcome_wall.blurb: Welcome Wall is a small bouldering outcrop on the east side of Bald Rock Basin in western Connecticut. It is among the first rocks you reach as you walk into the basin, a little downhill from the Pagan Rocks outcrops. It holds twelve boulder problems, from VB up to around V4, with the largest cluster at V3. Easier lines make it a friendly place to warm up, while the harder ones give a bit of a push. Since it sits near the basin entrance, it combines well with the other east side boulders for a longer session.

ct_king_boulder.blurb: King Boulder is a large single block with several distinct faces, tucked into the southwestern edge of the west side of Bald Rock Basin in Connecticut. Each side offers a different style of movement. The twelve problems range from V1 up to V8, and the weight of the grades lies in the middle and upper range, with a cluster around V5 and V6. That makes it a better stop for climbers who already boulder solidly than for beginners, though a few lower grades are there for warming up. Bring pads, since the faces are tall enough to want them.

ct_main_face.blurb: Main Face is the principal section of Great Ledge, a gneiss cliff on the Redding and Weston border in western Connecticut. The twelve climbs here are top ropes and trad lines. Grades start around 5.6 and run through 5.12, with a good group at 5.10. The wall is defined by a right-leaning crack, a big roof and a left-leaning weakness, which gives the face a varied set of challenges for a small crag. Chalk is common at the base. It suits climbers looking for steeper top rope and gear practice rather than easy mileage.

ct_9_wall_feather_ledges.blurb: 9 Wall is a small crag in the Feather Ledges area close to Chatfield Hollow State Park in Killingworth, Connecticut. The climbing is footwork-heavy, with a mix of trad, sport and top rope plus one hard boulder problem. Most of the twelve lines are around 5.9, with a few easier and harder ones mixed in, so it suits climbers who are comfortable at that level and happy to place some gear and clip a few bolts. Reaching the base takes a pleasant woods walk of roughly fifteen to twenty minutes.
ct_9_wall_feather_ledges.parking_note: Use the rough roadside pull-out on the south side of Route 80, about 0.3 miles west of the Chatfield Hollow State Park entrance.
ct_9_wall_feather_ledges.approach: From the pull-out, follow the old jeep trail south, then join the blue-blazed trail and stay with it past the junctions. The trail reaches the top of the crag first, then continues down to the base.
